issues.description: The Course initializer parameter order and labels in the solution do not match the constructor signature expected by the problem statement and the template. The problem statement and template show initializing Course using Course(name: ..., instructor: ..., ratings: ...), but the solution defines init(instructor: String, name: String, ratings: [Int]). This mismatch will cause compilation errors when client code calls Course(name:..., instructor:..., ratings:...) because the initializer's first parameter label in the solution is 'instructor' rather than 'name'.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course initializer parameter labels and order consistent with the problem statement and template by defining the initializer as init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) in the solution. Alternatively, update all client call sites to use the initializer parameter order and labels used in the solution (e.g., Course(instructor:..., name:..., ratings:...)), but aligning the solution initializer to name:, instructor:, ratings: is the recommended fix to match the exercise description and template.

issues.description: The initializer parameter ordering/labels for the Course class is inconsistent between the problem statement/template and the solution. The problem statement and the template show and expect Course(name: ..., instructor: ..., ratings: ...), but the solution implements init(instructor:name:ratings:). This mismatch (swapped parameter order/labels) creates confusion when students try to map the example call in the task to the actual initializer in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course initializer parameter labels and ordering consistent across all artifacts. For example, change the solution initializer to init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) so it matches the problem statement example Course(name: "My Course", instructor: "My Instructor", ratings: []).
